newsitem.title: UK: ADB eyes $1.0 bln 10-year global bond - dealers.
newsitem.headline: ADB eyes $1.0 bln 10-year global bond - dealers.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank is expected to launch a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond as soon as market conditions allow, new issues traders said on Thursday.
"There is a lot of talk about this deal and they are definitely planning on coming to market, especially as the new Japanese financial year has now begun," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
But he said the ADB was not convinced the 10-year sector was strong enough, with many investors still uncertain about the direction of U.S. interest rates.
Freddie Mac tapped the market on Wednesday with an $800 million 10-year bond, which was priced to yield 22 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note via Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan.
The spread had widened to 23.5 b.p. over on the bid side at 1430 GMT on Thursday.
Spread talk for an ADB deal was between 20 to 24 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, dealers said.
No mandate had yet been awarded, although it was likely a U.S. and a Japanese bank would be joint lead managers for the transaction.
